newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds move little ahead of U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds move little ahead of U.S. data.

text.p: Danish bond prices were marginally up on Thursday in a market with low activity and negligible movement waiting for U.S. May retail sales data.
"Activity is minimal and that is the way things look like staying until we get the American figures later this afternoon," one dealer said.

The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was up 0.07 point from the opening at 111.51, yielding 6.24 percent in one million crown turnover, while the forthcoming seven percent 2007 benchmark was up by the same amount at 104.13 and yielding 6.43 percent in turnover of 900 million crowns.
The 2006's June future was unchanged at 111.50 with 625 contracts traded. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 remained also unaltered at 89.90.
The crown traded at 3.8065 per mark at 1200 gmt, up a little from around 3.8070 at the start of trading.
The 2006 benchmark's 10-year yield gap with Germany narrowed one basis point to 46 from the opening with the 2007-bund differential also one point down at 65 bps.
